intro.text: A decaying city in Arelon. Everyone taken by the Shaod is sent there and forbidden to leave.
A decaying city in Arelon and the nation's capital before the Reod, surrounded by four smaller cities, Kae among them. Everyone taken by the Shaod is sent there and forbidden to leave.
A city in Arelon and the nation's capital before the Reod. Together with its four outer cities, Ake, Ato, Kae and Toa, it forms the shape of Aon Rao.

description.text: The palace, one of the city's largest buildings, stands at its exact center, with five domed wings crowned by spires; steps spiral up the central spire to a matchless view. The council chosen by the Elantrian elders to govern the city and its lands met there. Next to it is the university, a group of five or six long halls separated by open spaces. The bank lies in the market district, where merchants from across Opelon once gathered.
Elantris is counted among the most beautiful cities in the world, and sculptors in particular have heaped praise on its statues. Its name contains Aon Ela, meaning "center".

The Elantrians built a Korathi chapel in the city as a gesture of friendship to Teod, and it is said to be the finest of its kind; many find it surprising that beings worshipped as gods made room for another faith. Most rooms have metal plates bearing Aon Ashe to give light, and plates bearing Aon Tia were made to carry people instantly from one plate to another.

A hidden library lies beneath an Elantrian meetinghouse. Its door is marked with Aon Tae, but pressing the Aon works a set of gears rather than any magic. The Elantrians held the library sacred and banned AonDor inside it, and it is the only place in Elantris free of slime.

items.text: For centuries the Elantrians' AonDor had been the backbone of Arelon's economy, cheaply producing enough food to support huge urban populations. When Elantris fell, its loss helped throw Arelene society into turmoil and set off an uprising in which most Elantrians were killed by their own former servants. Iadon, once a successful merchant, rose to become king, moved most people onto plantations and made Kae, the only outer city still inhabited, the new capital.

Elantris was placed under quarantine. Anyone taken by the Shaod was sent into the city and never allowed out, and the only food that went in was the small pouch each newcomer received as part of Korathi funeral rites.

Inside, conditions kept getting worse. The city had been built with AonDor, and without it Elantris began to rot, its very stones crumbling. Elantrians no longer healed, and the pain of every injury built up until it drove them mad and they withdrew into themselves, endlessly repeating a single phrase as if in a trance. These Elantrians became known as the Hoed.
Karata's gang made its base in the palace, while Aanden's held the university and used its large library as a source of food.

The gangs, formed by Elantrians not yet Hoed, stole the food offerings of new arrivals, and Karata's also looked after the city's children. A third, savage gang based in the bank worshipped Shaor, in truth a little girl who had been thrown into the city wearing a wig and so seemed to have kept her hair.

Ten years after the Reod, the Shaod struck Raoden, Arelon's crown prince, and he was secretly sent into Elantris. Calling himself Spirit, he gathered followers, Karata among them, and set out to improve life in the city. They settled around an old Korathi chapel, scrubbed every surface clean of slime, streets included, and brought in the Hoed from the streets and alleys to look after them.
Over time Raoden also won over Aanden, who went back to his real name, Taan, and most of the gang leaders' followers joined him. The settlement came to be called New Elantris.

Raoden learned that the slime covering the city came from a mold that had grown as a thin, almost invisible film on every surface, feeding on the city's light and making it glow even brighter. When Elantris went dark, the mold died and rotted into brown slime.

Near the chapel, within New Elantris, stood the Roost, a large open-windowed building named for the birds carved on its walls. It was home to more than fifty Elantrian children and their caretaker, Matisse.
During the invasion of Arelon, Ashe took the Elantrian children to the hidden library to keep them safe.
